analysis_summary: The finding identifies explicit directory listing enabled via serveIndex middleware on the /ftp endpoint (line 288) of the publicly exposed 'juice' service. Code facts: (1) serveIndex('ftp', { icons: true }) is mounted at /ftp, enabling browser-based directory browsing; (2) /ftp files (excluding quarantine) are served publicly via servePublicFiles(); (3) /encryptionkeys (line 296) also has directory listing with view:'details'. Architecture facts: the service is publicly exposed, has high criticality, mixed authentication, and direct database access. Context priority is HIGH (7.0). Assumptions not yet verified: whether /ftp is accessible without authentication, what files exist in the directory, and whether the listing reveals sensitive file names or metadata. The /encryptionkeys listing is an additional concern beyond the flagged line.
risk_signals: Explicit serveIndex directory listing on /ftp of a publicly exposed high-criticality service
Mixed authentication model means /ftp may be unauthenticated
servePublicFiles() serves /ftp files without apparent auth gate
/encryptionkeys directory listing (line 296) with view:'details' exposes key file names and metadata
Context priority HIGH (7.0) due to public exposure, high criticality, and direct database access
